# dtcloud_lb (Resource)

Manages a load balancer -- the front door that accepts connections and the object every listener, pool and member hangs off.

A load balancer owns listeners, a listener owns a pool, and a pool owns members and at most one
health monitor. Each is a separate resource, so changing a health monitor does not disturb the
members.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Pick the size by name rather than pasting an id. Every name is offered twice --
# once without high availability and once with it -- so filter on both.
data "dtcloud_lb_flavors" "small" {
  name = "small"
  ha   = false
}

resource "dtcloud_lb" "public" {
  name        = "web-lb"
  description = "HTTPS front end for the web tier"
  flavor_id   = data.dtcloud_lb_flavors.small.flavors[0].id

  # Exactly one of vip_network_id, vip_subnet_id or vip_port_id decides where the
  # VIP lives. The platform enforces the same rule.
  vip_network_id = dtcloud_network.app.id
}
```

-> **The VIP anchor is exactly one of three.** `vip_network_id`, `vip_subnet_id` or `vip_port_id`
decides where the address lives. Declaring the rule here turns a server-side rejection into a
plan-time error.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `flavor_id` (String) ID of the load balancer flavor (sizing). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `name` (String) Name of the load balancer. Can be changed in place.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description. Can be changed in place.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the load balancer is administratively enabled.
- `external_network_id` (String) External network used when a floating IP is requested. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `floating_ip` (String) Floating IP to associate with the load balancer. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `network_type` (String) Network type. The API currently accepts only `Virtual`. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `vip_address` (String) Specific VIP address to request. Allocated by the platform when omitted. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `vip_network_id` (String) Network to place the VIP on. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `vip_port_id` (String) Existing port to use for the VIP. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `vip_subnet_id` (String) Subnet to place the VIP on. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Read-Only

- `balancing_pools` (Number) Number of balancing pools configured on the load balancer.
- `created_on` (String) When the load balancer was created, as reported by the API.
- `flavor_name` (String) Human-readable name of the flavor.
- `high_availability` (String) High-availability mode, reported as Enabled or Disabled. It is not settable here: HA is chosen by picking a flavor whose `ha` flag is true, so this reports back the flavor's setting.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `members_state` (List of String) Operating state of each member.
- `members_total` (Number) Total number of members across all pools.
- `network` (List of Object) The network the load balancer's VIP sits on. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network))
- `status` (String) Provisioning status, e.g. ACTIVE or ERROR.

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Only `name`, `description` and `enabled` change in place.** The VIP placement and the flavor are
  fixed at creation; changing either rebuilds the load balancer and everything hanging off it.
* **High availability is a property of the flavor.** There is no separate switch: each size is
  offered twice, once with `ha = false` and once with `ha = true`, and they are different flavors
  with different ids. Pick the HA one from `dtcloud_lb_flavors`.
* **The status vocabulary is the API's, not the raw platform's.** A load balancer reports one
  title-case word -- `Creating`, `Configuring`, `Active`, `Disabled`, `Deleting`, `Error` or
  `Unknown`. `Disabled` is a healthy load balancer with no listener yet, and `Unknown` is one with a
  pool but no health monitor; neither is a failure.
* **One change at a time.** The platform locks a load balancer while a change is in flight and
  refuses anything else until it settles. The provider waits for the lock and retries, which is what
  lets Terraform create a monitor and a member in parallel without either failing.
* **Do not mix the two styles.** Use the granular resources, or `dtcloud_lb_balancing_pool`, but not
  both on the same load balancer -- the granular resources would find objects they did not create.

## Timeouts

`create` defaults to 30 minutes, `update` and `delete` to 15. Creating, updating and deleting are all
asynchronous: the API answers at once and the provider polls until the load balancer settles.

## Import

```shell
terraform import dtcloud_lb.public 3d372446-4c75-4327-9511-98442456162f
```

`enabled` is not reported back, so an imported load balancer shows one in-place update that sets it
to whatever the configuration says, and is quiet from then on. The VIP anchor is recovered as the
network the address ended up on; if you anchored to a subnet or a port, say so in the configuration
after importing.
